title: Cap. IV Arg. 2 Sol: placere Deo = walk with God — without actual faith election would be temporal
pass_a_gloss: Further, those words, to please God, cannot be taken in one manner only. In the Pauline sense they indicate nothing else than to do works pleasing to God, or (as we noted from the original text) to walk with God. Now attend how dissonant it is, that no one could ever have been elected by God, unless he first have all those things without which our works cannot please God. Certainly without actual faith, I add also, and charity, no one can in this manner please God, (or what Enoch did) walk with God. If any force were in this argument, all election would be temporal, and would follow justification and sanctification.
pass_b_english: Further, to please God is not one sense only. Paulinely it means doing works pleasing to God, or (from the original) walking with God. Mark how absurd it is that no one could ever be elected unless he first has all that our works need to please God. Without actual faith — and charity too — no one can please God that way, or walk with God as Enoch did. If this argument had force, all election would be temporal and would follow justification and sanctification.
source_text: Dein, verba illa, placere Deo, non uno modo accipi possunt. Sensu Paulino nihil aliud indicant, quam facere opera Deo placentia, vel (ut ex originali textu notavimus) ambulare cum Deo. Jam attendite quam absonum sit, neminem potuisse unquam a Deo eligi, nisi prius ea omnia habeat sine quibus opera nostra Deo placere non possunt. Profecto absque fide actuali, addo etiam, et charitate, nemo potest hoc modo placere Deo, (aut quod Enochus fecit) cum Deo ambulare. Si ulla vis inesset huic argumento, electio omnis esset temporalis, et justificationem ac sanctificationem sequeretur.
